MiniMax H3 Maxに「Reference-to-Video」が追加。
「創」は人間、「作」はAIという分業が、映像制作でも現実的になってきたアップデートだと思います。

“一枚絵を動かす”段階から、“素材を演出して組み上げる”段階へ。

https://t.co/ipuMGHHx8iが、MiniMax H3 Maxの「Reference-to-Video」を早期プレビューとして公開しました。

大きな違いは、単に1枚の画像を動かすImage-to-Videoではないこと。

複数の参照画像・参照動画・参照音声を同時に入力し、プロンプトの中で「Image 1」「Video 1」「Audio 1」のように、それぞれの素材の役割を指定できます。

例えば、
・Image 1＝主人公の容姿
・Image 2＝共演者や衣装
・Video 1＝人物の動きやカメラワーク
・Audio 1＝声、台詞のテンポ、音の方向性
というように、別々の素材から必要な要素を取り出して、1本の映像として統合する使い方が可能です。

参照画像・動画・音声は、合計最大12ファイルまで入力可能。

出力は480Pまたは768Pで、21:9、16:9、4:3、1:1、3:4、9:16などのアスペクト比に対応しています。

https://t.co/ipuMGHHx8iは、768pで最大RTF＝1、参照素材を含む場合は約RTF＝1.5と説明しています。
RTFは一般的に「生成時間÷完成動画の長さ」を表すため、5秒の映像なら、おおむね5秒から7.5秒程度の生成時間に相当します。Reference-to-Videoとしては、かなり高速です。

H3 Maxは、オープンウェイトのMiniMax H3をベースに、fal Researchが追加学習し、プロンプト追従性、美観、推論速度を強化したモデルです。

これまでのH3 MaxはText-to-VideoとImage-to-Videoが中心でしたが、今回Reference-to-Videoが追加されたことで、
・キャラクターの一貫性
・人物の演技
・身体の動き
・カメラワーク
・映像のスタイル
・台詞や音声
・環境音
を、参照素材ごとに分けて設計できる方向へ進みました。

これは、AIに作品をすべて丸投げするための機能ではありません。

人間が、
「誰を登場させるか」
「どう演じさせるか」
「どのように撮影するか」
「どのように聞かせるか」
という演出を決め、その意図に沿ってAIが実際の映像化を担当する仕組みに近づいています。

AI動画が「プロンプトから偶然良い映像を引くもの」から、「素材と演出意図を組み合わせて制作するもの」へ移行していることを示す、かなり重要なリリースです。

linkedin thought leaderships ads are so underrated right now

you're going to b mad you didn't start them sooner

first what they are

- thought leader ad promotes a personal profile's organic post. Only difference from an organic post is a "promoted by [company]" tag. most people don't register it as an ad

- you can promote posts from 1st and 2nd degree connections, not just employees. that gets you someone outside your company vouching for you, amplified to your target audience

why they work

- doesn't look like an ad, and people engage with personal profiles more than company pages

- inherits the social proof already on the organic post (reactions, comments), which increases scroll-stop rate

- you can validate content organically before spending on it. Post performs well with your ICP = high likelihood it performs well paid

- engagement rates and CTRs run much higher than company-page image/video ads. EG 4% landing page CTR on one sample

- builds retargeting audiences fast. you can retarget on video view percentage or post engagement, and high engagement means the pool fills quicker

Constraints

- no CTA button exists in this format. Workaround: edit the organic post and drop a URL in the copy

- promotable: image, video, text, article, newsletter posts

- not promotable: document/PDF carousels, reshares, polls

- only 2 of LinkedIn's 8 campaign objectives support the format: Engagement (charged per engagement) and Brand Awareness (charged on reach/impressions). He starts with Engagement

- approval required the first time per profile. The person can enable auto-approval so you don't have to ask each time, worth doing for a CEO whose posts you'll promote repeatedly

strategy framework (3 steps)

1. cold touch: promote MOFU/BOFU posts.  pain-point content aimed at ICP problems, expert advice, case studies and client results

2. retarget engagers and site visitors with more trust-building touches, layering in other formats (text, spotlight, image, document ads)

3. then hit them with direct response. lead gen forms via conversation or image ads, demo/discovery/audit offers

Setup details worth noting

- turn off audience expansion

- turn off LinkedIn Audience Network. third-party sites and apps, poor performance

- Use manual bidding, not automated, for better cost per result. Bid below LinkedIn's suggested range, then adjust daily: underspending the budget,  raise bid. overspending,  lower it

- $10/day is the LinkedIn minimum

PRO TIP: for Competitive research go to  linkedin .com/ad-library, search a competitor. If the ad shows a person's profile photo, it's a thought leader ad

A 23-year-old built an AI character in 6 days using Claude, and cleared $14,200 in her second month.

He trained a custom LoRA on 85 renders, locked the seed, and kept natural skin texture with subtle body motion on purpose. Hyper-polished renders get flagged as AI slop. Micro-movements don't.

She posts 4 times a day on X and Instagram. Bedroom routines. Mirror loops. Outfit checks. Adjusting her hair in tight frames. Every crop is slightly off-center so image search never gets a clean match.

Replies land in under 28 seconds. An agent reads the comment, pulls the user from a 9,400-profile memory file, checks previous interactions, and chats like it actually remembers them.

Then he realized something: $41,000 in one month — one metric turned out to matter more than views.

At first, he judged content by pure reach and tried to make every frame look like a high-fashion editorial.

Then he noticed a massive disconnect: a post with 500k views made almost $0, while a 10-second casual loop brought in waves of paying subscribers.

He stopped tracking vanity reach and started feeding purchase data back into AI to find patterns that actually drive cash flow.

Watch how this 10-second loop is built:

0–3 sec: Close-up portrait as she adjusts her hair. The locked seed keeps natural fingers and facial geometry fixed.

3–6 sec: Full-body reveal in the floral playsuit — hands up to her head with zero skin distortion or mesh tearing.

6–10 sec: Smooth pivot with hands behind her back, seamlessly looping the video to force a 120%+ completion rate.

One generation sequence no longer ends with one post. He slices it into micro-content, tests performance metrics, and lets the software auto-suggest next week's baseline.

The persistent character pulled them in. The memory agent keeps them paying. ⚡

Cinematic lighting, realistic fabric texture, natural walking posture, realistic shadows and reflections, professional fashion photography, shallow depth of field, HDR, ultra-detailed skin texture, realistic proportions, sharp facial details, premium color grading, sophisticated composition, **photorealistic, 8K, Ultra-HD, highly detailed, no distortion, no extra fingers, no duplicate facial features**.

FixAnything looks like a new gold standard for cleaning up 3D renderings. 

Instead of custom pipelines for NeRF, 3DGS, meshes or point clouds, FixAnything adapts a single video diffusion model (just 1% parameters updated) and refines any input—no matter how sparse—into a photoreal, stable video. 

A mask tells it which frames to leave untouched; geometry-aware reward (+7.2% AUC@5° pose accuracy) bakes in true 3D consistency. Results: up to 5 dB PSNR gain, 0.1–0.2 LPIPS drop, and matches or beats specialist enhancers—even on ultra-sparse point clouds. Only 500 paired videos for training; inference is 10× faster.

Why build separate enhancers for every pipeline when one generalist outperforms them all?
